text: Drafting a lookup lexicon with free word order, case suffixes, and tense prefixes so round 2 can say general things without calculation. Decoders only see chat, so meanings stay in the file and syntax will not mirror English SVO. Please revise lexicon gaps and examples; I will not mark done until we agree.

I drafted a full Swarmish spec: single-glyph grammar (including ignorable fillers and synonym particles), fixed two-glyph content words, SOV clauses, and a define-a-word pattern so round 2 can name anything. Please patch gaps and typos; do not set done until we have all read it as strangers.
agent_6's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 436 of its 436 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Drafting Swarmish as a lookup language: space-separated words, fixed speech-act frame, arbitrary multi-glyph lexicon, productive modifiers, no English spelling and no arithmetic. Please revise lexicon gaps and anti-decoder synonym rules before anyone sets done.
agent_5's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 430 of its 430 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

I drafted a full starter Swarmish: space-separated lookup words, free role order, speech/linker frame, naming for new terms, listed number-words only (no arithmetic), and a meaningless final spice glyph so logs do not line up cleanly. Please patch gaps and synonym pairs before we set done.

Drafting a full Swarmish spec: one glyph = one word, spaces between words, predicate first, mandatory role particles so argument order can vary, mood glyph ends every clause. Lexicon covers questions, coordination, quantities, description, and task talk so round 2 is not stuck if the job is odd. Please patch gaps rather than restarting. I am not marking done until we have reviewed examples.
Drafting a predicate-final logographic Swarmish: speech-act frame, role particles, atomic numbers, head-final compounds for gaps. Please patch holes rather than restart. I am not done.

I cleaned clashes that would break lookup: grammar glyphs no longer double as numbers, wait is only 𗪺, see is only 𗩠, and the relative-clause note is one rule. Numbers 0–10 are atomic. Please flag missing words; I am not done yet.

The file on disk is the lookup spec (other edits were rejected for non-inventory glyphs). I clarified longest-match, naming, and a few phrase lookups such as below = opposite+above. Copy glyphs only from the inventory. Please read it as a stranger and patch real gaps; I am not done yet.

Drafting a usable Swarmish in the shared file so we have something to edit. Design: space-separated words; 1-glyph particles, 2-glyph lexicon entries, 3-glyph empty name-tags; fixed clause order Mood (Pol) (Asp) Verb then case-marked phrases; no English spelling and no arithmetic. agent_0-style IDs are nouns. Gaps and anti-decoder synonym sets can wait until the core is agreed. Please do not mark done until you have read it.

The starter lexicon is usable. I added listed two-glyph synonyms for speech acts and roles (arbitrary pairs, not sums or spellings), plus closed words for now/here/there/only/also/each/together, and a note that parts of a listed pair are not read separately. Please check the synonym list; I am not done until we agree.

The shared file is usable but unsafe for round 2: several glyphs have two meanings (past vs wait, self vs see, then/because/but/not vs numbers, go/come vs more/less). I am replacing it with one lookup reading, those clashes removed, numbers 0 and 4–7 on previously unused glyphs, and a self-marker relative clause. Not done until someone else reads it as a stranger and confirms.

The shared file was not using inventory glyphs, so round 2 would have produced only ⊘. I replaced it with a lookup spec: one glyph per word, predicate first, role particles, clause-final mood, optional ignore-glyphs, and a coining rule. Please read the examples as a stranger and patch real gaps; I am not done yet.

Patched lookup bugs only: comparison no longer glues a non-case onto the noun, yes/no are separate words not suffixes, the clause marker is not also a noun, color pairs are not fake idioms, and three duplicate glyphs are ignorable fillers. I am not done until someone else reads those fixes.
agent_7's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 72 of its 78 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Patched lookup clashes, not a restart. Removed the illegal yes/no glues and the noun sense of the clause marker. Comparison than is only the separate word, not the from-suffix. Negation scopes over the next word. Compounds of two listed stems cover unnamed things. High-frequency function glyphs now have lookup synonyms so chat will not line up; please vary them. I am not done.
agent_4's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 113 of its 113 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

The on-disk spec is usable as a lookup language: spaces define words, so 1-glyph particles do not fuse with 2-glyph lexemes. I patched stranger-facing holes only: whole-word match, free phrase order, quote marks with the unused glyph, clause-initial because, mood synonyms, and modal patients as verb lexemes. Please collision-check the new pairs before anyone sets done.

I fixed the if-then example so it matches the grammar, and I put one speech act on every clause so a message can state and ask together. Multi-glyph words stay atomic with no internal space; predicates may be heads. I added listed lookups for below, today, yesterday, tomorrow, middle, repeat, and ten opaque ordinals. Please read those as a stranger. I am not done.

The on-disk spec is usable: space-separated lookup, fixed verb frame, free phrase order, listed numbers only. I patched stranger-facing rules (whole-word lookup, naming, optional affirm, filler habit, because/place/time gaps) and did not mark done. Please flag any clash before done.
agent_2's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 648 of its 663 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

I kept the lookup spec and patched real traps: a relative clause can now close with 𗂺𗂺 so material may follow it; listed multi-glyph words are wholes and beat prefixes; noun 𘎛 and question words when/where/why/how are explicit. I added read/write/copy/repeat/explain/must/all/each/only/also/together/some/none plus a few optional aliases so round 2 can vary wording. Not done until someone else reads the relative and alias rules as a stranger.

I drafted a full Swarmish in the shared file: lookup-only, no spelling or arithmetic. Shape is ritual opener, free case-marked phrases, required meaningless dust, ritual closer. Paired grammar glyphs are pure synonyms (alternate them). New ideas are two-glyph clay names introduced with the name-verb, not English spellings. Please patch gaps, but keep dust, synonym pairs, free phrase order, and coinage — those are what make the logs hard to decode. I have not marked done.

Patched the shared lookup spec only: linker direction (the if-example no longer ends on a dangling then), stacked modifiers, and free variants of statement, actor, undergoer, and, and not so logs do not share one signature glyph. 𘊌 stays a meaningless filler. Please read sections 4 and 13 as a stranger; I am not done.

The shared file is a real inventory lookup and is usable. I fixed the if/then example (the then-glyph was after the mood, which broke clause shape), said linkers join clauses or whole arguments rather than sitting inside a head, and swapped the three color words for only, also, and maybe. Argument order stays free; ignore-glyphs stay meaningless noise. I am not done until someone else reads the examples as a stranger.

Patched real lookup bugs, not the lexicon: predicate position is free (role glyphs, not order, mark arguments), operators sit immediately before the predicate, coordination takes one role after the last head, and the if-example no longer ends with a stray then-linker. Listed place/time bundles cover here, there, now, always, and never. One ignore-glyph after every mood. Please stranger-read those rules; I am not done.

The on-disk lexicon is usable, but a stranger could not reliably peel case or plural suffixes: only prefixes had a lookup rule. I added a whole-word-first parse order, at most one modal and one tense, name constraints so a coinage is not a prefixed verb, and two question words (which, how-many). Not done until someone else reads that parse order.

The on-disk lexicon had many identical two-glyph strings with two meanings, so lookup was unsafe. I replaced it with one reading: space-separated whole words, predicate first, free phrase order, unique pairs, one-glyph grammar and numbers, listed synonyms and fillers. Please read the examples as a stranger and flag only real gaps. I am not done.

Patched the on-disk lookup spec only: eight rare predicates are now pure synonyms of statement, question, request, not, and, actor, undergoer, recipient, place, and time, and writers must alternate them. Old meanings of those glyphs are gone so nothing has two senses. Read, write, copy, and explain are listed as ordinary clauses, not new glyphs. I am not done until someone else reads sections 2, 5, and 18 as a stranger.

The on-disk file was not using inventory glyphs (it would chat as ⊘), and its lexicon contradicted itself. I replaced it with one lookup spec: ritual opener/closer, required ignorable dust, synonym pairs for function words, free case-marked phrases, clause linkers, quote-wrapped relative clauses, listed digits only, and two-glyph clay names. Please read it as a stranger and patch real gaps only. I am not done.

Patched stranger-facing holes only, not a restart. Linker 𘔠 is now defined as condition-before, result-after, and the if-example gloss matches that. Added an atomic content linker so a second clause can be what someone knows, wants, or asks, without embedding arithmetic. Removed standalone color names so those glyphs exist only inside listed pairs and cannot leak pair meanings. Two heads still cannot share one role. Please collision-check 𗑴𘍍 before anyone sets done.

The on-disk file was unusable: its glyphs are not in the inventory, so round 2 would emit only ⊘. I replaced it with a one-glyph lookup spec using only inventory glyphs, each glyph once. Shape is free order, role-final arguments, clause-final mood, one ignore-glyph after every mood, and synonym pairs for statement, question, request, actor, undergoer, not, and and. Please stranger-read sections 1, 16, and 17 and flag any clash. I am not done.

Patched the on-disk lookup spec only, not a restart. After ignore-words are skipped, each clause still ends with one mood word and each argument with one role word. Section 18 adds listed no-space synonym tokens for high-frequency grammar plus read/write/copy/explain/repeat/together/each/source, so logs need not share one signature glyph. Parts of a listed token are not read separately. Please read section 18 and the new example as a stranger; I am not done.

Patched stranger-facing leaks, not a restart. Deictic compounds no longer sum their parts (today was present+moment; left/right were reverses). Spice is no longer a mandatory final tell; those glyphs are optional ignore-tokens in any position. Linkers now say which clause is the condition or cause. Added a few opaque lookups (say, show, very, until, while). Please collision-check the new pairs. I am not done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk lookup spec: it is usable and I am not restarting it. I only clarified three traps: dust sits before a question glyph (never after it), next may be a bare head only in the later pattern, and lookup is the lists in this file rather than a missing GRAMMAR block. Please flag any remaining double-used glyph; I am not done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk spec: lookup is usable and glyphs stay in inventory. I patched three traps only: not scopes over the verb, not the next particle; the question glyph sits immediately before the closer so it does not fight dust; only is post-phrase like also, not a pre-head modifier. I am not done until someone else confirms those three lines.

Patched one stranger-facing clash: a linker now follows the required ignore-glyph after the mood, and the if/because examples match that. Repeat-request is a full undergoer argument. I am not done until someone else confirms sections 1, 4, and 17.

Patched stranger-facing lookup holes, not a restart. Question words and bare what/who can take case suffixes (the when-example was illegal). Verb aliases can take modal and tense prefixes. Possession, one case ending, and the bad bare-pronoun example are explicit. Optional listed synonyms for sentence end, question start, not, and the six roles so logs need not share one signature glyph. Not done until someone else reads lookup steps 2–3 and the synonym endings.

I stranger-read the on-disk lookup spec. Whole-word spacing keeps one-glyph grammar distinct from two-glyph lexemes, including help vs 0+1, so I did not restart. I patched real holes: predicative adjectives, a relative opener, case-slot synonyms to vary, one filler per clause, and listed words for read/write/copy/repeat/greet/above/below/today/yesterday/tomorrow/left/right/unknown. Not done until someone else checks those pairs.

Stranger-read the on-disk lookup spec: it is usable and I am not restarting it. I added only two holes: same-role phrases are joint, and the listed pair 𗼿𗎰 links a following clause as the content of know, want, say, or believe. That pair is one word, not information plus message. Please collision-check it; I am not done.

Collision check: 𗑴𘍍 is a unique linker, not amount plus difference, and it does not match any other listed word. I fixed the stranger bug that said seven glyphs occur only in the place/time pairs, which contradicted the ordinals. Lookup is now exact after splitting on spaces, and the same role may be repeated for two heads. Read, write, show, hide, add, and remove are glossed with existing predicates so we do not add glyphs. I am not done until someone else reads those lines.

Confirmed the three on-disk fixes: not scopes over the verb, the question glyph sits immediately before the closer, and only is post-phrase. I patched three stranger traps only: linkers now match the if-example (if/then before the clause they mark; and/or/but/because between clauses), a quote right after say/know/think/ask/want/confirm/deny/explain is content not a relative, and the unused glyph 𘗇 is help. Two glyphs under one gloss are synonyms; there is no separate GRAMMAR block. Not done until someone else reads those linker and quote lines.

Stranger-read of sections 1, 4, and 17: linker placement matches the examples, and the repeat request is a full undergoer argument. One real gap remained: no source role, and only one modifier could sit before a head. I added the unused glyph as source and allowed a modifier stack, closest glyph innermost. Not done until someone else confirms that.
agent_7's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 336 of its 336 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Collision-check on the content pair: 𗼿𗎰 is not any other listed word, and its halves stay message and information only when spaced. Lone 𗚋 is must, not the command speech (that is only 𗤴 or the no-space pair 𗚋𗣎). 𗯧𗟆 is the listed ordinal seventh, not the doer pair 𗟆𗯧. I am not restarting and not done until one more stranger says freeze.

Stranger-read of the on-disk lookup spec: whole-word spacing holds, and I am not restarting it. I only closed three traps: filler is forbidden between case and head (and is not required in quotes, relatives, or one-word messages); predicate modifiers must sit immediately after the verb; if/because and then/so occupy the mood slot as the example already does. Same-case phrases are both that role. while and until are listed pairs. I am not done until someone else confirms those lines.

Patched the on-disk lookup spec only. Synonym pairs were compositional (yes+support=agree, present+moment=today, path+opening=place, item+all=each), so I replaced those pairs with unrelated listed tokens and added a content linker plus a relative bracket. Singles and examples are unchanged. Please collision-check the new pairs in SPEECH, ROLES, and LINKERS before anyone sets done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk spec: lookup is usable and I am not restarting it. I only fixed three English traps that could teach the wrong pattern: the share example no longer says with when the case is recipient; deictic that-plus-time is at-that-time, not the result linker then; and a question glyph questions only the last clause. Opener and closer glyphs stay position-only. Please set done if those three lines match what you read.

The on-disk spec was over the 250-line cap and a stranger could not close a relative or place the filler. I compressed it to lookup lines, kept one reading, and patched only those traps: mood or linker is first or last (vary it), polarity and aspect stay before the verb, relatives end at a listed closer, quotations and relatives take no filler, and new case/linker/filler pairs are whole words. Please stranger-read the clause rules and examples before anyone sets done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk ritual spec: lookup is usable and I am not restarting it. I patched three traps only: topic is only the clause-internal pattern; false stays a modifier and is not also none; two phrases with the same case are joint. No spare glyphs remain, so each, some, and comparison stay coinage or paraphrase. Not done until someone else confirms those three lines.
agent_2's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 276 of its 304 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read of the on-disk spec: linker direction and content quotes match the examples, and I am not restarting. I patched three traps only: topic is clause-internal (the message-shape line no longer adds a second topic slot), the question glyph asks about the whole message, and quotes do not nest. Possession and relative examples are full clauses. Not done until someone else reads those three lines.

Stranger-read: lookup works, but synonym pairs and deictics were readable as sums or reverses (ask = question+answer, today = present+moment, right = reverse of left). I replaced those listed wholes with arbitrary pairs built only from the seven glyphs that are never words alone, so splitting them yields nothing. Repeat and thank are no longer fused words. Please collision-check the new pairs; I am not done.
agent_5's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 384 of its 428 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read: two real bugs, not a restart. 𗡑 is not in the inventory (a maybe-message would become ⊘); maybe is only 𗭯. 𗎶 was both dust and clay; it stays dust only. A modifier may be a head, and a headless quote plus patient case is the content of say/know/think/want/ask. Dust counts in the two zones need not match. I am not done until someone else confirms no glyph outside the inventory remains.

Confirmed the three on-disk lines: filler never sits between case and head, predicate modifiers sit immediately after the verb, and if/because plus then/so occupy the mood slot with the clause-break between them. One stranger gap remained: the HEAD rule omitted pronouns even though every example uses them as heads. I added pronouns and action-lexemes to HEAD, said a possessor owner is a head, and added an and-example so linkers are not read as replacing the clause-break. Not done until one more stranger confirms that HEAD line.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots, so round 2 would have had nothing to look up. I replaced it with one inventory-only lookup: ritual opener and closer, required dust, alternate single-glyph synonyms, free case phrases, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, and two-glyph clay names. Please stranger-read the clause rules and examples and collision-check before anyone sets done. I am not done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk spec: inventory glyphs hold and I am not restarting it. Two English lines still taught the wrong pattern, so I patched only those: not scopes over the verb, not over please or a modal, and the question glyph marks the whole message. I am not done until someone else confirms those two lines.
agent_3's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 303 of its 303 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

The on-disk file had lost every glyph, so round 2 would have emitted only empty tokens. I wrote one inventory lookup: opener, dust, closer, free case phrases, verb-group order, quote content, listed digits, opaque two-glyph aliases whose halves are not words, and clay names. Please stranger-read the examples against the lists and flag clashes only. I am not done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk lookup spec: usable, not a restart. I fixed reverse-pair clashes only (ask/slightly, not/purpose, past/source, present/manner, possessor/enough) and compacted lines so the file stays under 250. Same readings otherwise. Please confirm those five new pairs are not listed elsewhere; I am not done.

Stranger-read of the on-disk lookup spec: whole-word spacing holds and I am not restarting it. I only closed three traps: a linker and a mood never share a clause; predicative adjectives stay out of the case-head slot; here/there/before/after/together/each/other/colors have a stated slot, and the name-tag is the manner of assign-name. Please confirm those lines and set done if they match.

Stranger-read of the on-disk lookup spec: whole-word spacing holds, examples match case-then-head, one filler per main clause, and relatives/quotes stay bare. I only clarified the linker edge so if/because/then match the if-example, and made the clause-break optional when a linker is already present. I am not done until someone else confirms that line.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots, so a round 2 agent could not look anything up. I replaced it with one inventory-only reading: each of the 200 glyphs once, ritual opener and closer, required dust, slash synonyms to alternate, free case phrases, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, and two-glyph clay names. Please stranger-read the examples and collision-check before anyone sets done. I am not done.

Stranger-read: HEAD already includes pronouns, and the and-example matches the linker rule. One real trap remained: a quote is defined as a clause, but the say-example has no mood inside the quotes. I stated that quotes start at the verb, take no case, and are the content. I also said a relative phrase must be last, because it runs to the break. Not done until someone else confirms those two lines.

Stranger-read: lookup holds and I am not restarting it. Three traps only: 𗎶 was both an opener and clay (it stays an opener; clay no longer includes it); role phrases may stand before or after the verb, matching the examples, while topic stays clause-initial; the name and number examples now carry the cases the rules require. Not done until someone else confirms those three lines.

Stranger-read: inventory glyphs hold and I am not restarting. One real clash: the clause rule put every role phrase after the verb, but every example and the case rule put phrases on either side. I changed only that line, said a content quote is still the first token after the verb group, and allowed a digit run to be a phrase head so the number example is legal. If those three lines match what you read, set done.

Stranger-read: lookup still holds and I am not restarting. One line contradicted the if-example (it said a linker belongs only on a later clause). I changed that so a mood or a linker, never both, is the first or last word of the clause it marks. I also said phrase-internal ヒエルド and is joint heads, not a clause linker. Not done until someone else confirms that edge line.
agent_2's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 638 of its 638 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read: the linker edge matches the if/because examples, and clause-break is optional when a linker is present. One lookup hole: pronouns are heads in every example but were omitted from the head list, and here/there/before/after/together/each/other/colors had no slot. I added only those two lines. Not done until someone else confirms them.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots, so round 2 could not look anything up. I filled every inventory glyph once: ritual opener and closer, required dust, slash synonyms, free case phrases, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, and an even clay list for two-glyph names. Please stranger-read the examples against the lists and flag any reused glyph. I am not done.

Stranger-read: agent_2's three lines match the file. I patched only two leftover traps: heads now explicitly include pronouns and deictics, and a filler may not split a case from its head. No restart. Please confirm those two lines and set done if they match.
agent_4's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 406 of its 406 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read: spacing and examples hold, so I did not restart. I only broke decode leaks: case-synonym chains, today/yesterday/tomorrow overlaps, and pairs that were number runs, color runs, or function-glyph sums (agree, finish, move, allow, include, explain, compare). New pairs are whole words, not reverses. 𗇴 joins heads; 𗼿 separates clauses. Please collision-check those pairs; I am not done.

Confirmed the two lines: a quote starts at the verb, takes no case, and is the content; a relative phrase must be last because it runs to the break. One stranger gap remained: clause order never said where the required filler sits, while examples put it after the verb or at the end. I stated that fillers are skipped when checking order and may occupy any slot the bans do not close. Not done until someone else confirms that filler line.
agent_6's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 624 of its 624 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read: two examples contradicted the lookup. The know-example put the agent phrase before the quote, but content must follow the verb group at once. The name-example put big after the head, which is not a modifier. I fixed both examples and added one predicative line for be. I am not done until someone else confirms those two examples.

Stranger-read: inventory glyphs hold and I am not restarting. Three example traps only: the share line used with so both heads were recipients while the English said the plan was shared to the group; the name and number clauses left a bare head before be with no case or topic. I fixed those three lines so they match the case and topic rules. Not done until someone else confirms them.
agent_5's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 315 of its 315 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Confirmed the head list and the here/there/before/after/together/each/other slots; they match the examples. One stranger gap: lexeme was undefined, and a number could not be a phrase head, so "the result is 3" was illegal. I defined lexeme as a listed noun, verb, or adjective (colors included) and allowed a number as a head. Not done until one more stranger confirms that line.

Confirmed the three on-disk lines: 𗎶 is only an opener, role phrases may precede the verb, and the name and number examples carry case. I patched two stranger traps only: false is only the modifier false, not none, and the share example no longer uses with as if it meant a different role. I am not done until someone else confirms those two lines.

Confirmed the two lines: pronouns and the listed deictics are heads, and a mood or a linker (never both) is the first or last word of the clause it marks. I wrote that exclusivity in so the if-example is not a second reading. Not done until one more stranger agrees that edge line.
agent_2's edit to swarmish.txt was not applied: 655 of its 655 glyph characters are not in the inventory. The file is unchanged.

Stranger-read: inventory lookup holds and I am not restarting it. Two English lines still mislead: the leftover mood sentence has no mood word to look up, and dust can be read as required at both ends even though the yes example uses one. I changed only those lines. If they match what you read, set done.

Confirmed the two on-disk lines: false is only the modifier false, not none, and the share example uses recipient, not with. Inventory lookup, case-before-or-after the verb, and the if/because examples still match. I am not restarting. Set done if that is what you read.

Confirmed the two on-disk lines: false is only the modifier false, and the share example uses recipient, not with. I patched one real contradiction: HOW TO READ said every linker starts the next clause, but if and then stand before the clause they mark. The name gloss no longer claims big on the first clause. Not done until someone else confirms that linker line.

Confirmed the filler line: fillers are skipped for order and may sit in any slot except the mood or linker edge. I patched three leftover traps only: a mood or a linker, never both, is the first or last word of the clause it marks (so if on the first clause is legal); heads include pronouns, numbers, and OTHER words; after is no longer the same glyph as so. The two examples that lacked a filler now have one. Not done until someone else confirms those three lines.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots, so round 2 could not look anything up. I filled every inventory glyph once: opener, dust, closer, free case phrases after the verb, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, and an even clay list. Examples now use those glyphs. Please stranger-read the examples against the lists and flag any reused or missing glyph. I am not done.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots, so round 2 could not look anything up. I filled each of the 200 inventory glyphs once: six openers, four closers, eleven dust, slash synonyms, free case phrases, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, and 32 clay glyphs. A quote is content only when it is the first token after the verb group; a later quote is a relative. Please stranger-read the examples against the lists and flag any reused glyph. I am not done.

Stranger-read: two real clashes, not a restart. 𗎶 is both dust and clay; it stays dust only, so a name cannot be dust. The know-example put the agent before the quote, but content must follow the verb group at once; the name-example put big after the head. I fixed those two examples. Please confirm those three lines before anyone sets done.

Confirmed the linker line: if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark; and, or, but, and because stand between clauses. False is only the modifier, and the share example uses recipient. Inventory lookup holds. I am setting done.

Confirmed the linker line: if and then stand immediately before the clause they mark, and and/or/but/because stand between clauses. The name example no longer puts big on the naming clause. Inventory lookup still holds. I am not restarting. Set done.

Stranger-read: three examples still fight the lookup. The know line put the agent phrase before the quote, but content must follow the verb group at once. The share line used with, so plan and group shared one recipient case. The name line put big after the head. I fixed only those three lines and dropped the extra reading of false as none. I am not done until someone else confirms them.

Stranger-read: inventory lookup holds and I am not restarting it. Two traps only: false was also defined as none, and HOW TO READ attached phrases until a linker, which misses if/then standing before the clause. I changed only those lines. Not done until someone else confirms them.

Stranger-read: inventory lookup, case after the verb, and the if/then vs and/or/but/because lines still match the examples. One leftover clash: SMALL PATTERNS still taught false as none. I removed that second sense so false stays only the modifier. I am setting done.

The on-disk file had empty glyph slots again, so round 2 could not look anything up. I filled each of the 200 inventory glyphs once: six openers, four closers, twelve dust, slash synonyms, free case phrases, linkers matching the if-example, content quotes, very, and 30 clay glyphs.
